title.zh: 卷四十五 志第三十五 選舉志下
title.en: Volume 45 Treatises 40: Selecting and Appointing Officials 2
title.raw: 卷四十五 志第三十五 選舉志下 Volume 45 Treatises 40: Selecting and Appointing Officials 2

sentences.zh: 凡選有文、武，文選吏部主之，武選兵部主之，皆為三銓，尚書、侍郎分主之。

translations.literal: In general, selection had civil and military [branches]; civil selection was headed by the Ministry of Personnel, military selection by the Ministry of War; each was organized as three boards of evaluation, with ministers and vice-ministers dividing supervision among them.
translations.idiomatic: Selection was divided into civil and military tracks: the Ministry of Personnel oversaw civil appointments, the Ministry of War military ones. Each route used three evaluation boards, with ministers and vice-ministers taking charge in turn.

sentences.zh: 凡官員有數，而署置過者有罰，知而聽者有罰，規取者有罰。

translations.literal: In general, officials had fixed quotas; those who appointed beyond quota were punished, those who knowing allowed it were punished, those who schemed to obtain posts were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Every office had a fixed establishment. Appointing beyond that quota, knowingly permitting such over-appointment, or scheming to secure a post all carried penalties.

sentences.zh: 每歲五月，頒格於州縣，選人應格，則本屬或故任取選解，列其罷免、善惡之狀，以十月會於省，過其時者不敘。

translations.literal: Every year in the fifth month, standards were promulgated to prefectures and counties; when candidates met the standards, their current jurisdiction or former post would prepare a selection dossier, listing records of dismissal and commendation, and in the tenth month they would assemble at the capital—those past the deadline were not registered.
translations.idiomatic: Each year in the fifth month, qualification standards were issued to prefectures and counties. Candidates who met them had their home jurisdiction or former post prepare a selection dossier listing dismissals and merits, then convene at the capital in the tenth month; latecomers were not enrolled.

sentences.zh: 其以時至者，乃考其功過。

translations.literal: Those who arrived on time were then assessed for merits and faults.
translations.idiomatic: Only after candidates arrived on time were their merits and faults reviewed.

sentences.zh: 同流者，五五為聯，京官五人保之，一人識之。

translations.literal: Those of the same cohort were grouped in fives and tens; capital officials vouched for them in groups of five, one official attesting each group.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates of the same intake were grouped in fives and tens; five capital officials would jointly guarantee each group, with one official formally attesting it.

sentences.zh: 刑家之子、工賈異類及假名承偽、隱冒升降者有罰。

translations.literal: Sons of convicted families, artisans and merchants of alien categories, and those using false names, feigning succession, or concealing promotions and demotions were subject to punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of convicted households, artisans and merchants of disqualified categories, and anyone who used false names, feigned succession, or concealed promotions and demotions were liable to punishment.

sentences.zh: 文書粟錯，隱倖者駮放之；

translations.literal: Errors in documents and grain registers: if from concealed favoritism, reject and release;
translations.idiomatic: Errors in documents or grain accounts arising from concealed favoritism led to rejection and dismissal;

sentences.zh: 非隱倖則不。

translations.literal: if not from concealed favoritism, then not [so treated].
translations.idiomatic: if favoritism was not concealed, they were not.

sentences.zh: 凡擇人之法有四：一曰身，體貌豐偉；

translations.literal: In general, the methods for choosing men had four: first, body—physique stately and imposing;
translations.idiomatic: There were four criteria for assessing candidates: first, physique—a stately and imposing bearing;

sentences.zh: 二曰言，言辭辯正；

translations.literal: second, speech—words clear and correct;
translations.idiomatic: second, speech—clear and correct expression;

sentences.zh: 三曰書，楷法遒美；

translations.literal: third, writing—regular script forceful and beautiful;
translations.idiomatic: third, writing—forceful, beautiful regular script;

sentences.zh: 四曰判，文理優長。

translations.literal: fourth, judgment—literary reasoning outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: fourth, judgment—outstanding literary reasoning in written decisions.

sentences.zh: 四事皆可取，則先德行；

translations.literal: When all four matters could be taken, then virtue and conduct came first;
translations.idiomatic: When all four tests were passed, virtue and conduct took precedence;

sentences.zh: 德均以才，才均以勞。

translations.literal: equal in virtue, then by talent; equal in talent, then by seniority of service.
translations.idiomatic: if virtue was equal, talent decided; if talent was equal, length of service decided.

sentences.zh: 得者為留，不得者為放。

translations.literal: Those who passed were retained; those who did not were released.
translations.idiomatic: Those who qualified were retained; those who failed were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 五品以上不試，上其名中書門下；

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above were not examined; their names were submitted to the Secretariat and Chancellery;
translations.idiomatic: Officials of fifth rank and above were exempt from examination; their names went up to the Secretariat and Chancellery;

sentences.zh: 六品以下始集而試，觀其書、判。

translations.literal: Sixth rank and below first assembled for examination, observing their writing and judgments.
translations.idiomatic: those of sixth rank and below were first assembled for examination of their writing and judgment papers.

sentences.zh: 已試而銓，察其身、言；

translations.literal: After examination came evaluation, inspecting body and speech;
translations.idiomatic: After the written exam came board evaluation, inspecting physique and speech;

sentences.zh: 已銓而注，詢其便利而擬；

translations.literal: After evaluation came nomination, inquiring what was convenient and drafting [appointments];
translations.idiomatic: after evaluation came nomination, with posts proposed according to suitability;

sentences.zh: 已注而唱，不厭者得反通其辭，三唱而不厭，聽冬集。

translations.literal: After nomination came announcement; those not satisfied could state objections in return; three announcements without satisfaction allowed winter assembly.
translations.idiomatic: after nomination came public announcement; dissatisfied candidates could lodge objections, and after three announcements without acceptance they might wait for the winter intake.

sentences.zh: 厭者為甲，上於僕射，乃上門下省，給事中讀之，黃門侍郎省之，侍中審之，然後以聞。

translations.literal: Those satisfied formed the first list, submitted to the vice directors, then to the Department of State Affairs; drafting reviewers read it, vice ministers of the gate inspected it, the chief minister reviewed it, then it was reported.
translations.idiomatic: Accepted candidates formed the primary list, went to the vice directors, then to the Department of State Affairs, where drafting reviewers read it, vice ministers of the gate inspected it, the chief minister reviewed it, and only then was it reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 主者受旨而奉行焉，謂之「奏受」。

translations.literal: The responsible office received the decree and carried it out—this was called "memorial receipt."
translations.idiomatic: The responsible office received the imperial order and executed it—this was called "memorial receipt."

sentences.zh: 視品及流外，則判補。

translations.literal: For nominal rank and outside-the-stream posts, judgment [examination] determined supplementation.
translations.idiomatic: For nominal ranks and extra-stream posts, appointment was made by judgment examination alone.

sentences.zh: 皆給以符，謂之「告身」。

translations.literal: All were given tallies—called "appointment credentials."
translations.idiomatic: All received official tallies called "appointment credentials."

sentences.zh: 凡官已受成，皆廷謝。

translations.literal: In general, once offices were fully received, all gave court thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Once an appointment was fully confirmed, every appointee offered thanks at court.

sentences.zh: 凡試判登科謂之「入等」，甚拙者謂之「藍縷」。

translations.literal: In general, passing the judgment examination and entering the roster was called "entering the grade"; the very clumsy were called "ragged blue."
translations.idiomatic: Passing the judgment examination and making the roster was called "entering the grade"; very poor performances were called "ragged blue."

sentences.zh: 選未滿而試文三篇，謂之「宏辭」；

translations.literal: Before selection was complete, examining three literary compositions was called "grand rhetoric";
translations.idiomatic: Candidates not yet through regular selection who submitted three literary compositions took the "grand rhetoric" examination;

sentences.zh: 試判三條，謂之「拔萃」。

translations.literal: Examining three judgment items was called "outstanding selection."
translations.idiomatic: submitting three judgment papers took the "outstanding selection" examination.

sentences.zh: 中者即授官。

translations.literal: Those who passed were immediately granted office.
translations.idiomatic: Those who passed were appointed at once.

sentences.zh: 凡出身，嗣王、郡王，從四品下；

translations.literal: In general, for origins of office: heir apparent kings and commandery kings, lower supplementary fourth rank;
translations.idiomatic: By birth qualification: heirs apparent and commandery kings entered at lower supplementary fourth rank;

sentences.zh: 親王諸子封郡公者，從五品上；

translations.literal: sons of imperial princes enfeoffed as commandery dukes, upper supplementary fifth rank;
translations.idiomatic: sons of imperial princes enfeoffed as commandery dukes, upper supplementary fifth rank;

sentences.zh: 國公，正六品上；

translations.literal: state dukes, upper regular sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: state dukes, upper regular sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 郡公，正六品下；

translations.literal: commandery dukes, lower regular sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: commandery dukes, lower regular sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 縣公，從六品上；

translations.literal: county dukes, upper supplementary sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: county dukes, upper supplementary sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 侯，正七品上；

translations.literal: marquises, upper regular seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: marquises, upper regular seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 伯，正七品下；

translations.literal: earls, lower regular seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: earls, lower regular seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 子，從七品上；

translations.literal: viscounts, upper supplementary seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: viscounts, upper supplementary seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 男，從七品下；

translations.literal: barons, lower supplementary seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: barons, lower supplementary seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 皇帝緦麻以上親、皇太后期親，正六品上；

translations.literal: imperial kin within the highest mourning circle and the empress dowager's one-year mourning kin, upper regular sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: imperial relatives within the highest mourning circle and the empress dowager's one-year mourning kin, upper regular sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 皇太后大功、皇后期親，從六品上；

translations.literal: the empress dowager's second-grade mourning kin and the empress's one-year mourning kin, upper supplementary sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: the empress dowager's second-grade mourning kin and the empress's one-year mourning kin, upper supplementary sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 皇帝袒免、皇太后小功緦麻、皇后大功親，正七品上；

translations.literal: imperial kin in the bare-shoulder mourning grade, the empress dowager's third- and highest-grade mourning kin, and the empress's second-grade mourning kin, upper regular seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: imperial kin in the bare-shoulder mourning grade, the empress dowager's third- and highest-grade mourning kin, and the empress's second-grade mourning kin, upper regular seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 皇后小功緦麻、皇太子妃期親，從七品上。

translations.literal: the empress's third- and highest-grade mourning kin and the crown prince's consort's one-year mourning kin, upper supplementary seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: the empress's third- and highest-grade mourning kin and the crown prince's consort's one-year mourning kin, upper supplementary seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 外戚，皆以服屬降二階敘。

translations.literal: Maternal relatives by marriage were all registered two ranks lower according to mourning relation.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial affines were all registered two ranks lower according to their mourning relationship.

sentences.zh: 娶郡主者，正六品上；

translations.literal: those who married commandery princesses, upper regular sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Men who married commandery princesses, upper regular sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 娶縣主者，正七品上；

translations.literal: those who married county princesses, upper regular seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: men who married county princesses, upper regular seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 郡主子，從七品上；

translations.literal: sons of commandery princesses, upper supplementary seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: sons of commandery princesses, upper supplementary seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 縣主子，從八品上。

translations.literal: sons of county princesses, upper supplementary eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: sons of county princesses, upper supplementary eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 凡用廕，一品子，正七品上；

translations.literal: In general, for using yin privilege: sons of first rank, upper regular seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: By yin privilege: sons of first-rank officials, upper regular seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 二品子，正七品下；

translations.literal: sons of second rank, lower regular seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: sons of second rank, lower regular seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 三品子，從七品上；

translations.literal: sons of third rank, upper supplementary seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: sons of third rank, upper supplementary seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 從三品子，從七品下；

translations.literal: sons of supplementary third rank, lower supplementary seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: sons of supplementary third rank, lower supplementary seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 正四品子，正八品上；

translations.literal: sons of regular fourth rank, upper regular eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: sons of regular fourth rank, upper regular eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 從四品子，正八品下；

translations.literal: sons of supplementary fourth rank, lower regular eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: sons of supplementary fourth rank, lower regular eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 正五品子，從八品上；

translations.literal: sons of regular fifth rank, upper supplementary eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: sons of regular fifth rank, upper supplementary eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 從五品及國公子，從八品下。

translations.literal: sons of supplementary fifth rank and sons of state dukes, lower supplementary eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: sons of supplementary fifth rank and sons of state dukes, lower supplementary eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 凡品子任雜掌及王公以下親事、帳內勞滿而選者，七品以上子，從九品上敘。

translations.literal: In general, sons of ranked officials who served in miscellaneous clerical posts and princes' and dukes' household attendants and tent guards until service was complete and then selected—sons of seventh rank and above were registered at upper supplementary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of ranked officials who completed service as clerks, princely household attendants, or tent guards and then entered selection—if their fathers were seventh rank or above—were registered at upper supplementary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 其任流外而應入流內，敘品卑者，亦如之。

translations.literal: Those who served outside the stream and were due to enter within the stream, with lower registered rank, were treated the same.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had served outside the regular stream and were eligible to enter it, at the lower registered rank, followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 九品以上及勳官五品以上子，從九品下敘。

translations.literal: Sons of ninth rank and above and sons of merit officers of fifth rank and above were registered at lower supplementary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of officials of ninth rank and above and sons of merit officers of fifth rank and above were registered at lower supplementary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 三品以上廕曾孫，五品以上廕孫。

translations.literal: Yin great-grandsons for third rank and above; yin grandsons for fifth rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and above could extend yin privilege to great-grandsons; fifth rank and above to grandsons.

sentences.zh: 孫降子一等，曾孫降孫一等。

translations.literal: Grandsons were one grade lower than sons; great-grandsons one grade lower than grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Grandsons were registered one rank lower than sons; great-grandsons one rank lower than grandsons.

sentences.zh: 贈官降正官一等，死事者與正官同。

translations.literal: Posthumously conferred office was one grade lower than active office; those who died in service were treated the same as active office.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous offices counted one rank below the living rank, except for those who died in service, who were treated like active rank.

sentences.zh: 郡、縣公子，神從五品孫。

translations.literal: Sons of commandery and county dukes were rated as supplementary fifth-rank grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of commandery and county dukes were rated as supplementary fifth-rank grandsons.

sentences.zh: 縣男以上子，降一等。

translations.literal: Sons of county barons and above were lowered one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of county barons and higher titles were lowered one rank.

sentences.zh: 勳官二品子，又降一等。

translations.literal: Sons of second-rank merit officers were lowered yet another grade.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of second-rank merit officers were lowered another rank.

sentences.zh: 二王後孫，視正三品。

translations.literal: Grandsons of the two former dynasties were regarded as regular third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Grandsons of the two former dynasties were treated as regular third rank.

sentences.zh: 凡秀才，上上第，正八品上；

translations.literal: In general, for Xiucai: highest-highest grade, upper regular eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: For Xiucai graduates: highest tier, upper regular eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 上中第，正八品下；

translations.literal: upper-middle grade, lower regular eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: upper-middle tier, lower regular eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 上下第，從八品上；

translations.literal: upper-lower grade, upper supplementary eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: upper-lower tier, upper supplementary eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 中上第，從八品下。

translations.literal: middle-upper grade, lower supplementary eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: middle-upper tier, lower supplementary eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 明經，上上第，從八品下；

translations.literal: Mingjing: highest-highest grade, lower supplementary eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: For Mingjing graduates: highest tier, lower supplementary eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 上中第，正九品上；

translations.literal: upper-middle grade, upper regular ninth rank;
translations.idiomatic: upper-middle tier, upper regular ninth rank;

sentences.zh: 上下第，正九品下；

translations.literal: upper-lower grade, lower regular ninth rank;
translations.idiomatic: upper-lower tier, lower regular ninth rank;

sentences.zh: 中上第，從九品下。

translations.literal: middle-upper grade, lower supplementary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: middle-upper tier, lower supplementary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 進士、明法，甲第，從九品上；

translations.literal: Jinshi and Mingfa: first class, upper supplementary ninth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi and Mingfa graduates: class A, upper supplementary ninth rank;

sentences.zh: 乙第，從九品下。

translations.literal: second class, lower supplementary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: class B, lower supplementary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 弘文、崇文館生及第，亦如之。

translations.literal: Hongwen and Chongwen academy students who passed degrees were treated the same.
translations.idiomatic: Graduates of the Hongwen and Chongwen academies were registered the same way.

sentences.zh: 應入五品者，以聞。

translations.literal: Those due to enter fifth rank were reported.
translations.idiomatic: Cases warranting fifth rank or above were reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 書、算學生，從九品下敘。

translations.literal: Writing and calculation students were registered at lower supplementary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Students of writing and calculation were registered at lower supplementary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 凡弘文、崇文生，皇緦麻以上親，皇太后、皇后大功以上親，一家聽二人選。

translations.literal: In general, for Hongwen and Chongwen students: imperial kin within the highest mourning circle, the empress dowager's and empress's second-grade mourning kin and above—one household was allowed two selections.
translations.idiomatic: For Hongwen and Chongwen students: imperial kin within the highest mourning circle, and the empress dowager's and empress's second-grade mourning kin and closer—each household could send two candidates.

sentences.zh: 職事二品以上、散官一品、中書門下正三品同三品、六尚書等子孫並侄，功臣身食實封者子孫，一廕聽二人選。

translations.literal: Active officials of second rank and above, honorary first rank, Secretariat and Chancellery regular third rank treated as third rank, the six ministers' sons and grandsons and nephews, and sons and grandsons of merit holders receiving substantive fiefs—one yin privilege allowed two selections.
translations.idiomatic: Active officials of second rank and above, honorary first rank, Secretariat regular third rank treated as third rank, sons and nephews of the six ministers, and descendants of merit holders with substantive fiefs—each yin privilege allowed two selections.

sentences.zh: 京官職事正三品、同中書門下平章事、供奉官三品子孫，京官職事從三品、中書黃門侍郎並供奉三品官、帶四品五品散官子，一廕一人。

translations.literal: Capital active officials of regular third rank, those equal to Secretariat and Chancellery chief ministers, and sons and grandsons of third-rank palace attendants; capital active supplementary third rank, Secretariat and Gate vice ministers and third-rank attendants, and sons bearing fourth- or fifth-rank honorary rank—one yin privilege allowed one person.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials of regular third rank, chief ministers, and third-rank palace attendants' descendants; supplementary third rank, Secretariat and Gate vice ministers, third-rank attendants, and sons bearing fourth- or fifth-rank honorary titles—each yin privilege allowed one candidate.

sentences.zh: 凡勳官選者，上柱國，正六品敘；

translations.literal: In general, for merit officer selection: Upper Pillar of the State, registered at regular sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: For merit officers entering selection: Upper Pillar of the State, regular sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 六品而下，遞降一階。

translations.literal: from sixth rank downward, each step lowered one grade.
translations.idiomatic: from sixth rank downward, each title lowered one rank.

sentences.zh: 驍騎尉、武騎尉，從九品上敘。

translations.literal: Valiant Cavalry Commandant and Martial Cavalry Commandant, registered at upper supplementary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Valiant Cavalry and Martial Cavalry commandants were registered at upper supplementary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 凡居官必四考，四考中中，進年勞一階敘。

translations.literal: In general, holding office required four evaluations; four evaluations at middle-middle advanced one grade in seniority per year of service.
translations.idiomatic: Holding office required four performance reviews; four reviews at middle-middle advanced one seniority step per year served.

sentences.zh: 每一考，中上進一階，上下二階，上中以上及計考應至五品以上奏而別敘。

translations.literal: Each evaluation: middle-upper advanced one grade, upper-lower two grades; upper-middle and above and cumulative evaluations reaching fifth rank and above were memorialized and registered separately.
translations.idiomatic: Each review: middle-upper gained one step, upper-lower two steps; upper-middle and above, and cumulative reviews reaching fifth rank, were reported separately for special registration.

sentences.zh: 六品以下遷改不更選及守五品以上官，年勞歲一敘，給記階牒。

translations.literal: Sixth rank and below transferred without re-selection and those holding fifth rank and above registered seniority once yearly, issuing step-record documents.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of sixth rank and below transferred without re-selection, and those holding fifth rank and above, had seniority registered yearly and received step-record documents.

sentences.zh: 考多者，准考累加。

translations.literal: Those with many evaluations were allowed to accumulate evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: Extra evaluations could be accumulated toward advancement.

sentences.zh: 凡醫術，不過尚藥奉禦。

translations.literal: In general, for medical skill, no higher than Court Physician for Imperial Medicines.
translations.idiomatic: Physicians could rise no higher than Court Physician for Imperial Medicines.

sentences.zh: 陰陽、卜筮、圖畫、工巧、造食、音聲及天文，不過本色局、署令。

translations.literal: Yin-yang masters, diviners, painters, artisans, food preparers, musicians, and astronomers could not exceed director of their native bureau or office.
translations.idiomatic: Yin-yang specialists, diviners, painters, artisans, cooks, musicians, and astronomers could not rise above director of their own bureau.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚譯語，不過典客署令。

translations.literal: Honglu translators could not exceed Director of the Bureau of Receptions.
translations.idiomatic: Honglu interpreters could not rise above Director of the Bureau of Receptions.

sentences.zh: 凡千牛備身、備身左右，五考送兵部試，有文者送吏部。

translations.literal: In general, Thousand-Ox Guards and Left and Right Bodyguards, after five evaluations were sent to the Ministry of War for examination; those with literary skill were sent to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-Ox guards and left and right bodyguards, after five reviews, were sent to the Ministry of War for examination; literate candidates went to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 凡齋郎，太廟以五品以上子孫及六品職事並清官子為之，六考而滿；

translations.literal: In general, acolytes: the Imperial Ancestral Temple took sons and grandsons of fifth rank and above and sons of sixth-rank active officials and pure officials, completing service in six evaluations;
translations.idiomatic: Temple acolytes for the Imperial Ancestral Temple were drawn from sons of fifth rank and above and sons of sixth-rank active or pure officials, with service complete after six reviews;

sentences.zh: 郊社以六品職事官子為之，八考而滿。

translations.literal: Suburban and Altar temples took sons of sixth-rank active officials, completing service in eight evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban and Altar temples took sons of sixth-rank active officials, with service complete after eight reviews.

sentences.zh: 皆讀兩經粗通，限年十五以上、二十以下，擇儀狀端正無疾者。

translations.literal: All had to read two classics with rough comprehension, limited to ages fifteen and above and twenty and below, choosing those of proper bearing, upright appearance, and without illness.
translations.idiomatic: All had to show rough mastery of two classics, be between fifteen and twenty, and be chosen for proper bearing, good appearance, and sound health.

sentences.zh: 武選，凡納課品子，歲取文武六品以下、勳官三品以下五品以上子，年十八以上，每州為解上兵部，納課十三歲而試，第一等送吏部，第二等留本司，第三等納資二歲，第四等納資三歲；

translations.literal: Military selection: in general, for tuition-paying sons of ranked families, each year were taken sons of civil and military sixth rank and below and sons of merit officers from supplementary third rank to fifth rank and above, age eighteen and above; each prefecture submitted dossiers to the Ministry of War; after thirteen years of tuition payment came examination—first grade sent to Ministry of Personnel, second grade kept in this ministry, third grade paid two years' fees, fourth grade paid three years' fees;
translations.idiomatic: For military selection, tuition-paying sons of ranked families: each year sons of civil and military officials of sixth rank and below, and sons of merit officers from supplementary third through fifth rank, aged eighteen or above, were nominated by prefecture to the Ministry of War. After thirteen years of tuition they were examined: first class went to the Ministry of Personnel, second stayed with the Ministry of War, third paid two years' fees, fourth paid three years' fees;

sentences.zh: 納已，復試，量文武授散官。

translations.literal: Once fees were paid, they were re-examined and civil or military honorary rank was granted according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: After fees were paid, they were re-examined and granted honorary civil or military rank as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 若考滿不試，免當年資；

translations.literal: If service was complete but they did not take the examination, that year's seniority credit was waived;
translations.idiomatic: If service was complete but they skipped the exam, that year's seniority credit was forfeited;

sentences.zh: 遭喪免資。

translations.literal: mourning exempted fee payment.
translations.idiomatic: mourning exempted fee payment.

sentences.zh: 無故不輸資及有犯者，放還之。

translations.literal: Those who without cause did not pay fees or who committed offenses were released and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Those who failed to pay fees without cause, or who committed offenses, were dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 凡捉錢品子，無違負滿二百日，本屬以簿附朝集使，上於考功、兵部。

translations.literal: In general, for money-lending sons of ranked families, when without default for two hundred full days, the home jurisdiction attached the register to the capital assembly envoy and submitted it to the Ministry of Merit and the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: For money-lending sons of ranked families, after two hundred days without default, the home jurisdiction forwarded the register with the capital assembly envoy to the Ministries of Merit and War.

sentences.zh: 滿十歲，量文武授散官。

translations.literal: After ten full years, civil or military honorary rank was granted according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years, they were assessed and granted honorary civil or military rank.

sentences.zh: 其視品國官府佐應停者，依品子納課，十歲而試，凡一歲為一選。

translations.literal: Those nominal-rank state and princely household aides due to be dismissed followed ranked sons in paying tuition, were examined at ten years, and each year counted as one selection round.
translations.idiomatic: Nominal-rank aides in state and princely offices slated for dismissal paid tuition like ranked sons, were examined at ten years, with one selection round per year.

sentences.zh: 自一選至十二選，視官品高下以定其數，因其功過而增損之。

translations.literal: From one selection round to twelve, the number was set according to official rank high and low, increased or decreased according to merits and faults.
translations.idiomatic: From one to twelve selection rounds, the required number depended on official rank and was adjusted for merit or fault.

sentences.zh: 初，武德中，天下兵革新定，士不求祿，官不充員。

translations.literal: At first, in the Wude era, when military revolution had just settled the realm, scholars did not seek stipends and offices were not filled to quota.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude reign, with the realm newly settled after war, scholars did not seek office and posts went unfilled.

sentences.zh: 有司移符州縣，課人赴調，遠方或賜衣續食，猶辭不行。

translations.literal: The responsible offices sent orders to prefectures and counties to press men to come for selection; distant regions might be given clothing and travel provisions, yet they still declined to go.
translations.idiomatic: Authorities ordered prefectures and counties to send candidates; distant regions might receive clothing and travel rations, yet many still refused to come.

sentences.zh: 至則授用，無所黜退。

translations.literal: When they arrived they were appointed and used, with no dismissal or rejection.
translations.idiomatic: Those who came were appointed outright, with no screening out.

sentences.zh: 不數年，求者浸多，亦頗加簡汰。

translations.literal: Within a few years, seekers gradually increased, and selection also became somewhat stricter.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years applicants multiplied, and the process grew somewhat more selective.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，侍郎劉林甫言：「隋制以十一月為選始，至春乃畢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan, Vice Minister Liu Linpu said: "The Sui system took the eleventh month as the start of selection, finishing only in spring.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 2, Vice Minister Liu Linpu said: "Under the Sui, selection began in the eleventh month and did not finish until spring.

sentences.zh: 今選者眾，請四時注擬。」

translations.literal: Now candidates are numerous; please nominate appointments in all four seasons."
translations.idiomatic: Candidates are now too numerous; please allow nominations in all four seasons.

sentences.zh: 十九年，馬周以四時選為勞，乃復以十一月選，至三月畢。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, Ma Zhou held year-round selection too burdensome, and selection was again set from the eleventh month, finishing by the third month.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19, Ma Zhou argued that year-round selection was too burdensome, so selection again ran from the eleventh month through the third month.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗謂攝吏部尚書杜如晦曰：「今專以言辭刀筆取人，而不悉其行，至後敗職，雖刑戮之，而民已敝矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong once said to acting Minister of Personnel Du Ruhui: "Now we take men solely by words and brushwork, without fully knowing their conduct; when later they fail in office, even if we punish them by law, the people are already exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong once told acting Minister of Personnel Du Ruhui: "We now choose men only by eloquence and paperwork, without truly knowing their conduct. When they later fail in office, even execution cannot undo the harm already done to the people.

sentences.zh: 乃欲放古，令諸州辟召。

translations.literal: He then wished to return to antiquity and have the prefectures summon and appoint.
translations.idiomatic: He then wished to revive the ancient practice of prefectural recruitment.

sentences.zh: 會功臣行世封，乃止。

translations.literal: It happened that merit holders were enfeoffed for generations, and the plan stopped.
translations.idiomatic: But when merit holders received hereditary fiefs, the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 它日復顧侍臣曰：「致治之術，在於得賢。

translations.literal: Another day he again turned to his attendants and said: "The art of bringing order lies in obtaining the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Another day he told his attendants: "Good government depends on finding worthy men.

sentences.zh: 今公等不知人，朕又不能遍識，日月其逝，而人遠矣。

translations.literal: Now you gentlemen do not know men, and I too cannot know them all; the sun and moon pass on, and worthy men grow distant.
translations.idiomatic: You do not know men, and I cannot know them all either. Days pass, and worthy men slip away.

sentences.zh: 吾將使人自舉，可乎？」

translations.literal: I will have men recommend themselves—is that acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: Shall I let men recommend themselves?

sentences.zh: 而魏徵以為長澆競，又止。

translations.literal: But Wei Zheng held that this would long encourage contentious rivalry, and it stopped again.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng argued it would only encourage empty rivalry, and the idea was dropped again.

sentences.zh: 初，銓法簡而任重。

translations.literal: At first, evaluation law was simple yet weighty in responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: At first the evaluation system was simple but carried real weight.

sentences.zh: 高宗總章二年，司列少常伯裴行儉始設長名榜，引銓注法，復定州縣升降為八等，其三京、五府、都護、都督府，悉有差次，量官資授之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zongzhang under Emperor Gaozong, Director of the Bureau of Appointments Pei Xingjian first established the long-name roster, applying nomination law, again fixing prefectures and counties in eight grades of promotion and demotion; the three capitals, five prefectures, protectorates, and area commands all had sequences, and offices were granted according to qualifications.
translations.idiomatic: In Gaozong's Zongzhang 2, Pei Xingjian created the long-name roster and nomination rules, ranked prefectures and counties in eight grades, and set posting sequences for the capitals, major prefectures, protectorates, and area commands according to rank and seniority.

sentences.zh: 其後李敬玄為少常伯，委事于員外郎張仁禕，仁禕又造姓曆，改狀樣、銓曆等程式，而銓總之法密矣。

translations.literal: Later Li Jingxuan became director and entrusted affairs to aide Zhang Renyi; Renyi also created surname registers, changed dossier forms, evaluation calendars, and other procedures, and the methods of overall evaluation grew intricate.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Jingxuan delegated the work to Zhang Renyi, who devised surname registers and revised dossiers and evaluation schedules until the system grew highly intricate.

sentences.zh: 然是時仕者眾，庸愚鹹集，有偽主符告而矯為官者，有接承它名而參調者，有遠人無親而置保者。

translations.literal: Yet at this time office-seekers were numerous, the mediocre and foolish all gathered; some forged appointment tallies and pretended to be officials, some took others' names to join selection, some distant men without kin set up guarantors.
translations.idiomatic: Yet office-seekers crowded in: some forged credentials, some entered under others' names, and some distant candidates without kin arranged false guarantors.

sentences.zh: 試之日，冒名代進，或旁坐假手，或借人外助，多非其實。

translations.literal: On examination day, they entered under false names, or sat beside and used another's hand, or borrowed outside help—mostly not genuine.
translations.idiomatic: On exam day many submitted under false names, had others write for them, or used outside help—most entries were fraudulent.

sentences.zh: 雖繁設等級、遞差選限、增譴犯之科、開糾告之令以遏之，然猶不能禁。

translations.literal: Although they multiplied grades, staggered selection limits, increased penalties for violations, and opened orders for denunciation to restrain it, still they could not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: Though the state multiplied grades, staggered selection limits, stiffened penalties, and encouraged denunciation, abuse could not be stopped.

sentences.zh: 大率十人競一官，餘多委積不可遣，有司患之，謀為黜落之計，以僻書隱學為判目，無復求人之意。

translations.literal: Roughly ten men competed for one office; the rest piled up and could not be dispatched. The offices worried and plotted a plan of rejection, making obscure books and hidden learning the judgment topics, with no further intent of seeking men.
translations.idiomatic: Roughly ten men competed for each post; the rest piled up unplaceable. Frustrated officials sought to weed candidates out by testing obscure scholarship, no longer trying to find talent.

sentences.zh: 而吏求貨賄，出入升降。

translations.literal: Yet clerks sought bribes, controlling advancement and demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks took bribes and controlled who rose or fell.

sentences.zh: 至武后時，天官侍郎魏玄同深嫉之，因請復古辟署之法，不報。

translations.literal: By Empress Wu's time, Vice Minister of the Bureau of Celestial Offices Wei Xuantong deeply resented this and requested restoring the ancient method of summons and appointment, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, Vice Minister Wei Xuantong deplored this and asked to restore ancient prefectural recruitment, but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 初，試選人皆糊名，令學士考判，武后以為非委任之方，罷之。

translations.literal: At first, examination candidates were all name-sealed, with academicians grading judgments; Empress Wu held this not the way of true appointment and abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: At first exam papers were sealed and graded by academicians; Empress Wu thought that was not true appointment and ended the practice.

sentences.zh: 而其務收人心，士無賢不肖，多所進獎。

translations.literal: Yet her task was winning hearts; whether scholars were worthy or not, many were advanced and rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: She sought popular support instead, advancing and rewarding candidates regardless of merit.

sentences.zh: 長安二年，舉人授拾遺、補闕、御史、著作佐郎、大理評事、衛佐凡百餘人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chang'an, examination graduates were given Reminder, Supplementation, Censor, Assistant Archivist, Court Reviewer, and Guard Aide posts—more than a hundred men in all.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an 2, more than a hundred graduates were appointed Reminders, Supplementation officials, censors, assistant archivists, court reviewers, and guard aides.

sentences.zh: 明年，引見風俗使，舉人悉授試官，高者至鳳閣舍人、給事中，次員外郎、御史、補闕、拾遺、校書郎。

translations.literal: The next year, presented to the Commissioner of Customs, all graduates were given provisional offices; the highest reached Phoenix Pavilion Attendant or Drafting Reviewer, next aide, censor, supplementation, reminder, and collator.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, after presentation to the customs commissioner, all graduates received provisional posts, up to Phoenix Pavilion attendant or drafting reviewer, then aide, censor, supplementation, reminder, or collator.

sentences.zh: 試官之起，自此始。

translations.literal: The rise of provisional officials began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Provisional appointments began here.

sentences.zh: 時李嶠為尚書，又置員外郎二千餘員，悉用勢家親戚，給俸祿，使厘務，至與正官爭事相毆者。

translations.literal: At the time Li Qiao was minister and also set up more than two thousand aide posts, all using powerful families' kin, giving salaries and having them handle affairs, even to the point of fighting regular officials over business.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiao then created more than two thousand aide posts for powerful families' relatives, paid them salaries, and set them to work—some even brawled with regular officials over duties.

sentences.zh: 又有檢校、敕攝、判知之官。

translations.literal: There were also inspecting, edict-assigned, and acting-supervisor posts.
translations.idiomatic: There were also inspecting, edict-assigned, and acting-supervisor posts.

sentences.zh: 神龍二年，嶠復為中書令，始悔之，乃停員外官厘務。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenlong, Qiao again became Secretariat Director, began to regret it, and stopped aide officials from handling affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong 2, Li Qiao again became Secretariat Director, regretted the abuse, and barred aide officials from handling regular duties.

sentences.zh: 中宗時，韋後及太平、安樂公主等用事，於側門降墨敕斜封授官，號「斜封官」，凡數千員。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Zhongzong, Empress Wei and the Princesses of Peace and of Peaceful Joy held power; at the side gate they issued ink edicts with slanted seals to grant office—called "slanted-seal officials"—several thousand posts in all.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhongzong, Empress Wei and the Princesses Taiping and Anle ruled through side-gate edicts with slanted seals, creating thousands of "slanted-seal" appointees.

sentences.zh: 內外盈溢，無聽事以居，當時謂之「三無坐處」，言宰相、御史及員外郎也。

translations.literal: Inside and outside overflowed; there were no offices to sit in. The age called it "three offices with nowhere to sit," meaning chancellors, censors, and aides.
translations.idiomatic: Offices overflowed so that chancellors, censors, and aides had nowhere to sit—the age called it "three offices with no seat."

sentences.zh: 又以鄭愔為侍郎，大納貨賂，選人留者甚眾，至逆用三年員闕，而綱紀大潰。

translations.literal: Zheng Yin was again made vice minister, greatly accepting bribes; candidates detained were very numerous, even using three years of vacant posts in reverse, and discipline greatly collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yin as vice minister took huge bribes, detained masses of candidates, and even filled posts three years in advance, collapsing the system.

sentences.zh: 韋氏敗，始以宋璟為吏部尚書，李乂、盧從願為侍郎，姚元之為兵部尚書，陸象先、盧懷慎為侍郎，悉奏罷斜封官，量闕留人，雖資高考深，非才實者不取。

translations.literal: When the Wei clan fell, Song Jing was first made Minister of Personnel, Li Yi and Lu Congyuan vice ministers, Yao Yuanzhi Minister of War, Lu Xiangxian and Lu Huaiqian vice ministers; all memorialized to abolish slanted-seal officials, measured vacancies and retained men; though seniority was high and examination deep, those without real talent were not taken.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei clan's fall, Song Jing, Li Yi, Lu Congyuan, Yao Yuanzhi, Lu Xiangxian, and Lu Huaiqian abolished slanted-seal posts, matched vacancies to candidates, and refused men of high seniority but no real ability.

sentences.zh: 初，尚書銓掌七品以上選，侍郎銓掌八品以下選。

translations.literal: At first the minister evaluated selection for seventh rank and above; vice ministers evaluated eighth rank and below.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the minister handled selection for seventh rank and above, vice ministers for eighth rank and below.

sentences.zh: 至是，通其品而掌焉。

translations.literal: At this point ranks were unified and they managed all.
translations.idiomatic: Now they handled all ranks together.

sentences.zh: 未幾，璟、元之等罷，殿中侍御史崔涖、太子中允薛昭希太平公主意，上言：「罷斜封官，人失其所，而怨積於下，必有非常之變。」

translations.literal: Before long Jing, Yuanzhi, and others were dismissed; Palace Censor Cui Li and Crown Prince Attendant Xue Zhao, pleasing Princess Taiping, submitted: "Abolishing slanted-seal officials, men lose their place, resentment accumulates below, and there will surely be extraordinary change."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Song and Yao were dismissed; Cui Li and Xue Zhao, courting Princess Taiping, warned: "Abolishing slanted-seal posts leaves men displaced, resentment builds below, and disaster will follow.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔盡復斜封別敕官。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued fully restoring slanted-seal and special-edict officials.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then fully restored slanted-seal and special-edict appointments.

sentences.zh: 玄宗即位，厲精為治。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, he applied himself diligently to governance.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong took the throne, he threw himself into reform.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺內供奉張九齡上疏言：「縣令、刺史，陛下所與共理，尤親於民者也。

translations.literal: Left Reminder and Inner Attendant Zhang Jiuling submitted: "Magistrates and prefects are those Your Majesty governs with—especially close to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling submitted: "Magistrates and prefects are Your Majesty's partners in governing the people.

sentences.zh: 今京官出外，乃反以為斥逐，非少重其選不可。」

translations.literal: Now when capital officials go out, it is instead taken as banishment; selection for these posts cannot but be made weightier."
translations.idiomatic: Yet capital officials treat local posts as exile; their selection must be taken more seriously.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「古者或遙聞辟召，或一見任之，是以士脩名行，而流品不雜。

translations.literal: He also said: "In antiquity men were sometimes summoned from afar on reputation, sometimes appointed at a single meeting; thus scholars cultivated conduct and rank was not mixed.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "In antiquity men were recruited by reputation or appointed at first meeting, so scholars cultivated conduct and ranks stayed pure.

sentences.zh: 今吏部始造簿書，以備遺忘，而反求精於案牘，不急人才，何異遺劍中流，而刻舟以記。」

translations.literal: Now the Ministry of Personnel first makes ledgers to guard against forgetting, yet instead seeks precision in documents, not urgently seeking talent—how is this different from losing a sword in midstream yet marking the boat to remember?"
translations.idiomatic: Now the Ministry keeps ledgers against forgetfulness yet prizes paperwork over talent—like marking the boat after losing a sword in the river.

sentences.zh: 於是下詔擇京官有善政者補刺史，歲十月，按察使校殿最，自第一至第五，校考使及戶部長官總核之，以為升降。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued choosing capital officials with good administration to fill prefect posts; each year in the tenth month investigating commissioners graded excellence from first to fifth, and review commissioners with the head of the Ministry of Revenue totaled them for promotion and demotion.
translations.idiomatic: The throne then chose capital officials with good records for prefectures; each tenth month investigators graded them from first to fifth rank, and review commissioners with the revenue chief determined promotions.

sentences.zh: 凡官，不曆州縣不擬台省。

translations.literal: In general, officials who had not served in prefectures and counties were not nominated for central departments.
translations.idiomatic: In general, officials who had not served locally were not nominated for central posts.

sentences.zh: 已而悉集新除縣令宣政殿，親臨問以治人之策，而擢其高第者。

translations.literal: Soon all newly appointed magistrates were gathered in the Hall of Proclaiming Governance; the emperor personally questioned them on policies for governing men and promoted those of highest grade.
translations.idiomatic: He then assembled new magistrates in the Hall of Proclaiming Governance, questioned them on governance, and promoted the best answers.

sentences.zh: 又詔員外郎、御史諸供奉官，皆進名敕授，而兵、吏部各以員外郎一人判南曹，由是銓司之任輕矣。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered that aide officials, censors, and all palace attendants advance names for edict appointment; the Ministries of War and Personnel each had one aide judge the southern registry, and thus the evaluation offices' duties grew lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Aides, censors, and palace attendants were ordered to submit names for direct appointment; each of the war and personnel ministries assigned one aide to the southern registry, lightening the evaluation offices' role.

sentences.zh: 其後戶部侍郎宇文融又建議置十銓，乃以禮部尚書蘇頲等分主之。

translations.literal: Later Vice Minister of Revenue Yuwen Rong again proposed establishing ten evaluation boards, and Minister of Rites Su Ting and others were assigned to divide supervision.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuwen Rong proposed ten evaluation boards, with Su Ting and others placed in charge.

sentences.zh: 太子左庶子吳兢諫曰：「《易》稱'君子思不出其位'，言不侵官也。

translations.literal: Left Companion of the Heir Apparent Wu Jing remonstrated: "The Changes says 'the noble man does not think beyond his post'—meaning one should not invade another's office.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jing remonstrated: "The Changes says the noble man does not think beyond his post—one must not usurp another's duties.

sentences.zh: 今以頲等分掌吏部選，而天子親臨決之，尚書、侍郎皆不聞參，議者以為萬乘之君，下行選事。」

translations.literal: Now Ting and others divide control of Personnel selection while the Son of Heaven personally decides—minister and vice ministers all unheard from; critics held that the lord of ten thousand chariots was personally conducting selection below."
translations.idiomatic: Now Su Ting and others run personnel selection while the emperor decides in person, leaving minister and vice ministers out—critics said the Son of Heaven was doing clerks' work.

sentences.zh: 帝悟，遂復以三銓還有司。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and returned the three evaluation boards to the regular offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the point and restored the three boards to the regular ministries.

sentences.zh: 開元十八年，侍中裴光庭兼吏部尚書，始作循資格，而賢愚一概，必與格合，乃得銓授，限年躡級，不得逾越。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Kaiyuan, Chief Minister Pei Guangting also served as Minister of Personnel and first made seniority regulations; worthy and foolish were treated alike—one had to match the regulation to receive evaluation appointment, years limited step by step, none could overstep.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 18, Pei Guangting as chief minister and personnel minister introduced seniority rules: worthy and unworthy alike had to match the schedule, advancing rank by rank without skipping years.

sentences.zh: 於是久淹不收者皆便之，謂之「聖書」。

translations.literal: Thus those long detained without appointment all found it convenient and called it the "sage's writ."
translations.idiomatic: Long-stalled candidates welcomed it and called it the "sage's writ."

sentences.zh: 及光庭卒，中書令蕭嵩以為非求材之方，奏罷之。

translations.literal: When Guangting died, Secretariat Director Xiao Song held it not the way to seek talent and memorialized to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangting died, Xiao Song argued it was not a way to find talent and had it abolished.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：「凡人年三十而出身，四十乃得從事，更造格以分寸為差，若循新格，則六十未離一尉。

translations.literal: An edict was issued: "Ordinary men enter office at thirty and may begin active service at forty; remade regulations differ by minute grades—if one follows the new regulation, at sixty one has not yet left a captaincy.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Men normally enter service at thirty and take active posts at forty; under the new minute grades, a man might still be a captain at sixty.

sentences.zh: 自今選人才業優異有操行及遠郡下寮名跡稍著者，吏部隨材甄擢之。」

translations.literal: From now in selection, those of outstanding talent and conduct, and lower aides in distant commanderies whose names and traces are somewhat notable—the Ministry of Personnel shall select and promote according to ability."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the Ministry of Personnel should promote candidates of outstanding talent, conduct, or local reputation without waiting on the schedule."

sentences.zh: 初，諸司官兼知政事者，至日午後乃還本司視事。

translations.literal: At first, officials of various offices who also handled state affairs returned to their home offices to conduct business only after noon.
translations.idiomatic: At first officials who also handled state affairs returned to their home ministries only after noon.

sentences.zh: 兵部、吏部尚書侍郎知政事者，亦還本司分闕注唱。

translations.literal: Ministers and vice ministers of War and Personnel who handled state affairs also returned to their offices to divide vacancies, nominate, and announce.
translations.idiomatic: War and personnel ministers who handled state affairs likewise returned to divide vacancies, nominate, and announce appointments.

sentences.zh: 開元以來，宰相位望漸崇，雖尚書知政事，亦於中書決本司事以自便。

translations.literal: Since Kaiyuan, chancellors' standing gradually rose; even ministers handling state affairs decided their home office business at the Secretariat for convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Since Kaiyuan, chancellors' status rose; even personnel ministers decided their ministry's business at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 而左、右相兼兵部、吏部尚書者，不自銓總。

translations.literal: Yet left and right chancellors who also served as war or personnel ministers did not personally oversee evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Left and right chancellors who also headed war or personnel did not personally run evaluation.

sentences.zh: 又故事，必三銓、三注、三唱而後擬官，季春始畢，乃過門下省。

translations.literal: By precedent, there had to be three evaluations, three nominations, and three announcements before drafting office; only late spring was it finished, then it passed the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent three evaluations, nominations, and announcements preceded appointment, finishing only in late spring before passing the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠以右相兼文部尚書，建議選人視官資、書判、狀跡、功優，宜對眾定留放。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong as right chancellor and literary minister proposed that candidates, viewing qualifications, judgment papers, dossier records, and merit, should have retention or release decided before the public.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong as right chancellor and literary minister proposed deciding retention publicly from qualifications, judgment papers, records, and merit.

sentences.zh: 乃先遣吏密定員闕，一日會左相及諸司長官于都堂注唱，以誇神速。

translations.literal: He first sent clerks secretly to fix vacant posts, then in one day gathered the left chancellor and heads of offices in the capital hall for nomination and announcement, to boast of speed.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks secretly fixed vacancies beforehand; in one day he gathered chancellors and bureau heads in the capital hall to announce appointments and boast of speed.

sentences.zh: 由是門下過官、三銓注官之制皆廢，侍郎主試判而已。

translations.literal: Thus the Department of State Affairs' review of officials and the three-board nomination system were all abolished; vice ministers handled judgment examinations only.
translations.idiomatic: Department review and the three-board nomination system were abolished; vice ministers handled judgment exams only.

sentences.zh: 肅、代以後兵興，天下多故，官員益濫，而銓法無可道者。

translations.literal: After Suzong and Daizong, war arose, the realm had many troubles, officials grew ever more excessive, and evaluation law had nothing worth stating.
translations.idiomatic: After Suzong and Daizong, war and turmoil multiplied officials until evaluation law collapsed entirely.

sentences.zh: 至德宗時，試太常寺協律郎沈既濟極言其敝曰：

translations.literal: By Emperor Dezong's time, probationary Harmonizing Officer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Shen Jiji spoke fully of its abuses, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Under Dezong, Shen Jiji, a probationary harmonizing officer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, denounced the abuses at length:

sentences.zh: 近世爵祿失之者久，其失非他，四太而已：入仕之門太多，世胄之家太優，祿利之資太厚，督責之令太薄。

translations.literal: In recent times rank and stipend have long been lost; the loss is nothing else but four excesses: too many gates into office, noble houses too favored, salary benefits too thick, oversight commands too thin.
translations.idiomatic: Rank and salary have long been corrupted by four excesses: too many paths to office, too much favor for noble houses, salaries too rich, and oversight too weak.

sentences.zh: 臣以為當輕其祿利，重其督責。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that salary benefits should be lightened and oversight made heavy.
translations.idiomatic: I believe salaries should be reduced and oversight strengthened.

sentences.zh: 夫古今選用之法，九流常敘，有三科而已，曰德也，才也，勞也；

translations.literal: The methods of selection and appointment ancient and modern, the regular order of the nine currents, have only three categories: virtue, talent, and service;
translations.idiomatic: Ancient and modern selection rests on three standards: virtue, talent, and service;

sentences.zh: 而今選曹，皆不及焉。

translations.literal: yet today's selection office reaches none of them.
translations.idiomatic: yet today's selection office reaches none of them.

sentences.zh: 且吏部甲令，雖曰度德居任，量才授職，計勞升敘，然考校之法，皆在書判簿曆、言辭俯仰之間，侍郎非通神，不可得而知。

translations.literal: Moreover, though Personnel regulations say to measure virtue for appointment, measure talent for office, and count service for promotion, the methods of examination all lie between judgment papers, ledgers, and the rise and fall of words—vice ministers are not divine and cannot know.
translations.idiomatic: Though regulations speak of virtue, talent, and service, examination rests on paperwork and mannerisms—no vice minister can truly know a man's worth.

sentences.zh: 則安行徐言，非德也；

translations.literal: Then calm walking and slow speech are not virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Calm bearing and slow speech are not virtue;

sentences.zh: 空文善書，非才也；

translations.literal: empty writing and skillful script are not talent;
translations.idiomatic: fluent prose and fine calligraphy are not talent;

sentences.zh: 累資積考，非勞也。

translations.literal: accumulated seniority and piled evaluations are not service.
translations.idiomatic: stacked seniority and evaluations are not service.

sentences.zh: 苟執不失，猶乖得人，況眾流茫茫，耳目有不足者乎？

translations.literal: If one clings without error, one still misses obtaining men—how much more when the many currents are boundless and eyes and ears are insufficient?
translations.idiomatic: Even rigid adherence misses the right men, let alone when countless candidates overwhelm human judgment.

sentences.zh: 蓋非鑒之不明，非擇之不精，法使然也。

translations.literal: It is not that the mirror is unclear or the choice not precise—the law makes it so.
translations.idiomatic: The fault lies not in poor judgment but in the law itself.

sentences.zh: 王者觀變以制法，察時而立政。

translations.literal: The king observes change to make law and examines the times to establish policy.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler must read change to make law and read the times to set policy.

sentences.zh: 按前代選用，皆州、府察舉，至於齊、隋，署置多由請托。

translations.literal: Examining former ages' selection and appointment, all were investigated and recommended by prefectures and districts; by Qi and Sui, appointments mostly came through requests and patronage.
translations.idiomatic: Former ages relied on prefectural recommendation; by Qi and Sui appointments came mostly through patronage.

sentences.zh: 故當時議者，以為與其率私，不若自舉；

translations.literal: Thus critics of the time held that rather than follow private ties, it was better to self-recommend;
translations.idiomatic: Critics then said: better self-recommendation than private favoritism;

sentences.zh: 與其外濫，不若內收。

translations.literal: rather than external excess, better internal collection.
translations.idiomatic: better central control than outside abuse.

sentences.zh: 是以罷州府之權，而歸於吏部。

translations.literal: Therefore prefectural power was abolished and returned to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: So prefectural power was withdrawn and centralized in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 此矯時懲弊之權法，非經國不刊之常典。

translations.literal: This was a provisional law to correct the times and punish abuses, not an immutable constant for governing the state.
translations.idiomatic: That was a temporary remedy, not an eternal statecraft.

sentences.zh: 今吏部之法蹙矣，不可以坐守刓弊。

translations.literal: Now Personnel law is cramped and one cannot sit guarding carved-out abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel law is now cramped; we cannot cling to a failing system.

sentences.zh: 臣請五品以上及群司長官、宰臣進敘，吏部、兵部得參議焉；

translations.literal: Your subject requests that fifth rank and above and heads of offices and chancellors advance nominations, with Ministries of Personnel and War allowed to join deliberation;
translations.idiomatic: I propose that fifth rank and above, bureau heads, and chancellors nominate candidates, with personnel and war ministries consulting;

sentences.zh: 六品以下或僚佐之屬，聽州、府辟用。

translations.literal: sixth rank and below or the class of aides and assistants may be summoned and employed by prefectures and districts.
translations.idiomatic: sixth rank and below and aides may be recruited by prefectures.

sentences.zh: 則銓擇之任，委于四方；

translations.literal: Then the duty of evaluation and choice is entrusted to the four quarters;
translations.idiomatic: Evaluation would rest with the regions;

sentences.zh: 結奏之成，歸於二部。

translations.literal: the completion of summary memorials returns to the two ministries.
translations.idiomatic: final approval would return to the two ministries.

sentences.zh: 必先擇牧守，然後授其權。

translations.literal: One must first choose governors and prefects, then grant them authority.
translations.idiomatic: Choose good governors first, then grant them authority.

sentences.zh: 高者先署而後聞，卑者聽版而不命。

translations.literal: Higher posts are first signed then reported; lower ones hear the board without edict.
translations.idiomatic: Higher posts would be signed locally then reported; lower ones confirmed by board without edict.

sentences.zh: 其牧守、將帥，或選用非公，則吏部、兵部得察而舉之。

translations.literal: If governors, prefects, or generals select and employ not impartially, the Ministries of Personnel and War may investigate and impeach.
translations.idiomatic: If governors or generals appoint unfairly, personnel and war ministries may investigate and impeach.

sentences.zh: 聖主明目達聰，逖聽遐視，罪其私冒。

translations.literal: The sage ruler's eyes are bright and ears penetrating, listening far and seeing afar, punishing private usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: The sage ruler sees and hears afar and punishes private abuse.

sentences.zh: 不慎舉者，小加譴黜，大正刑典。

translations.literal: Those not careful in recommendation receive small censure and demotion; great cases are corrected by the penal code.
translations.idiomatic: Careless recommenders face censure or criminal punishment.

sentences.zh: 責成授任，誰敢不勉？

translations.literal: Charge them with fulfillment of appointment—who dares not strive?
translations.idiomatic: Hold appointees accountable—who would not strive?

sentences.zh: 夫如是，則接名偽命之徒，菲才薄行之人，貪叨賄貨，懦弱奸宄，下詔之日，隨聲而廢，通大數，十去八九矣。

translations.literal: If so, then those who seize names and fake appointments, men of slight talent and thin conduct, the greedy who take bribes, the weak and treacherous—on the day the edict descends they would be abolished with the sound; by the general count, eight or nine of ten would go.
translations.idiomatic: Then name-seizers, mediocrity, bribe-takers, and the weak or treacherous would vanish at the edict's promulgation—eight or nine in ten of today's abuses.

sentences.zh: 如是，人少而員寬，事核而官審，賢者不獎而自進，不肖者不抑而自退。

translations.literal: If so, men are few and posts ample, affairs examined and offices careful; the worthy advance without reward, the unworthy withdraw without suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Then posts would be ample, duties clear, the worthy would rise unbidden, and the unworthy would withdraw on their own.

sentences.zh: 或曰：'開元、天寶中，不易吏部之法，而天下砥平，何必外辟，方臻於理？

translations.literal: Someone said: "In the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, without changing Personnel law, the realm was leveled like a whetstone—why must one recruit outside to reach good order?"
translations.idiomatic: Some objected: "Under Kaiyuan and Tianbao the realm was at peace without changing personnel law—why recruit outside to achieve good order?"

sentences.zh: '臣以為不然。

translations.literal: "Your subject holds this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: I disagree.

sentences.zh: 夫選舉者，經邦之一端，雖制之有美惡，而行之由法令。

translations.literal: Selection and appointment are one aspect of governing the state; though the system has beauty and ugliness, its execution depends on statutes and orders.
translations.idiomatic: Selection is one pillar of statecraft; systems may be good or bad, but results depend on how laws are enforced.

sentences.zh: 是以州郡察舉，在兩漢則理，在魏、齊則亂。

translations.literal: Thus prefectural investigation and recommendation was orderly in the two Han dynasties and chaotic in Wei and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural recommendation worked in the two Han dynasties but failed in Wei and Qi.

sentences.zh: 吏部選集，在神龍、景龍則紊，在開元、天寶則理。

translations.literal: Personnel assembly and selection was disorderly in Shenlong and Jinglong and orderly in Kaiyuan and Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: Centralized personnel selection failed under Shenlong and Jinglong but succeeded under Kaiyuan and Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 當其時久承升平，禦以法術，慶賞不軼，威刑必齊，由是而理，匪用吏部而臻此也。

translations.literal: At that time, long enjoying rising peace, governed by law and method, rewards not missed, awe and punishment all aligned—order came from this, not from using Personnel to reach it.
translations.idiomatic: Those eras enjoyed long peace, firm law, timely rewards, and even punishments—order came from governance itself, not from the personnel system alone.

sentences.zh: 向以此時用辟召之法，則理不益久乎？」

translations.literal: Had summons and appointment been used then, would order not have lasted even longer?"
translations.idiomatic: Had recruitment been used then, would order not have lasted even longer?"

sentences.zh: 天子雖嘉其言，而重於改作，訖不能用。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven though praising his words, weighed reform heavily and in the end could not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him but feared sweeping reform and never adopted the plan.

sentences.zh: 初，吏部歲常集人，其後三數歲一集，選人猥至，文簿紛雜，吏因得以為奸利，士至蹉跌，或十年不得官，而闕員亦累歲不補。

translations.literal: At first the Ministry of Personnel annually assembled candidates; later it assembled every few years. Candidates crowded in, documents piled in confusion, clerks thus gained illicit profit, scholars stumbled—some ten years without office—while vacant posts also went years unfilled.
translations.idiomatic: At first personnel held annual assemblies, then only every few years. Crowds of candidates and chaotic paperwork let clerks profit; some scholars waited ten years for office while vacancies went unfilled for years.

sentences.zh: 陸贄為相，乃懲其弊，命吏部據內外員三分之，計闕集人，歲以為常。

translations.literal: When Lu Zhi became chancellor, he punished these abuses and ordered Personnel to take one-third of internal and external posts, count vacancies, and assemble candidates yearly as the rule.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Lu Zhi reformed the abuse, ordering personnel to fill one-third of posts annually according to vacancies.

sentences.zh: 是時，河西、隴右沒于虜，河南、河北不上計，吏員大率減天寶三之一，而入流者加一，故士人二年居官，十年待選，而考限遷除之法浸壞。

translations.literal: At this time Hexi and Longyou fell to barbarians; Henan and Hebei sent no accounts. Official posts were roughly reduced by one-third from Tianbao levels while those entering the stream increased by one; thus scholars held office two years and waited for selection ten, and the law of evaluation limits and promotion gradually broke down.
translations.idiomatic: With Hexi and Longyou lost and the north in turmoil, posts fell by a third from Tianbao levels while candidates doubled; scholars served two years but waited ten for promotion, and review laws decayed.

sentences.zh: 憲宗時，宰相李吉甫定考遷之格，諸州刺史、次赤府少尹、次赤令、諸陵令、五府司馬、上州以上上佐、東宮官詹事諭德以下、王府官四品以上皆五考。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xianzong, Chancellor Li Jifu fixed grades for evaluation and transfer: prefects of all prefectures, vice governors of secondary capitals, magistrates of secondary capitals, tomb directors, five-capital marshals, senior aides of upper prefectures and above, Eastern Palace officials from grand tutor and moral instructor downward, and princely household officials of fourth rank and above—all five evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianzong, Li Jifu set review standards: prefects, secondary-capital officials, tomb directors, capital marshals, senior prefectural aides, Eastern Palace staff from grand tutor down, and fourth-rank princely officials—all required five reviews.

sentences.zh: 侍御史十三月，殿中侍御史十八月，監察御史二十五月。

translations.literal: Attending censor thirteen months, palace attending censor eighteen months, investigating censor twenty-five months.
translations.idiomatic: Attending censors thirteen months, palace attending censors eighteen, investigating censors twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 三省官、諸道敕補、檢校五品以上及台省官皆三考，餘官四考，文武官四品以下五考。

translations.literal: Three-department officials, circuit edict supplements, inspecting fifth rank and above, and secretariat and department officials all three evaluations; other offices four evaluations; civil and military fourth rank and below five evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: Three-department officials, circuit appointees, inspecting fifth rank and above, and secretariat staff took three reviews; other offices four; civil and military fourth rank and below five.

sentences.zh: 凡遷，尚書省四品以上、文武官三品以上皆先奏。

translations.literal: In general for transfers, Secretariat fourth rank and above and civil and military third rank and above were all memorialized first.
translations.idiomatic: Transfers of secretariat fourth rank and above and third-rank civil or military officials required prior memorial.

sentences.zh: 唐取人之路蓋多矣，方其盛時，著於令者，納課品子萬人，諸館及州縣學六萬三千七十人，太史曆生三十六人，天文生百五十人，太醫藥童、針咒諸生二百一十一人，太卜卜筮三十人，千牛備身八十人，備身左右二百五十六人，進馬十六人，齋郎八百六十二人，諸衛三衛監門直長三萬九千四百六十二人，諸屯主、副千九百八人，諸折沖府錄事、府、史一千七百八十二人，校尉三千五百六十四人，執仗、執乘每府三十二人，親事、帳內萬人，集賢院禦書手百人，史館典書、楷書四十一人，尚藥童三十人，諸台、省、寺、監、軍、衛、坊、府之胥史六千餘人。

translations.literal: Tang paths for obtaining men were many indeed. At its height, recorded in statutes: tuition-paying sons of ranked families ten thousand; academy and prefectural and county school students sixty-three thousand seventy; Grand Astrologer calendar students thirty-six; astronomy students one hundred fifty; Imperial Medical pharmacy youths, acupuncture and incantation students two hundred eleven; Grand Diviner divination students thirty; Thousand-Ox guards eighty; left and right bodyguards two hundred fifty-six; presenting-horse officers sixteen; acolytes eight hundred sixty-two; guard directors of the three guards and gatekeepers thirty-nine thousand four hundred sixty-two; garrison chiefs and deputies one thousand nine hundred eight; area-command recorders, aides, and clerks one thousand seven hundred eighty-two; commandants three thousand five hundred sixty-four; halberd and carriage bearers thirty-two per command; personal attendants and tent guards ten thousand; Imperial Library copyists one hundred; Historiography archive collators and copyists forty-one; Imperial Pharmacy youths thirty; clerks of departments, ministries, directorates, commissions, armies, guards, wards, and offices more than six thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Tang had many paths to office. At its height, statutes recorded: ten thousand tuition-paying sons of ranked families; sixty-three thousand academy and local school students; thirty-six calendar students; one hundred fifty astronomy students; two hundred eleven medical, acupuncture, and incantation students; thirty diviners; eighty Thousand-Ox guards; two hundred fifty-six bodyguards; sixteen presenting-horse officers; eight hundred sixty-two acolytes; nearly forty thousand guard and gate officers; nearly two thousand garrison chiefs; nearly eighteen hundred area-command clerks; three thousand five hundred commandants; halberd and carriage bearers in each command; ten thousand personal and tent attendants; one hundred imperial library copyists; forty-one historiography clerks; thirty pharmacy youths; and more than six thousand clerks across the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 凡此者，皆入官之門戶，而諸司主錄已成官及州縣佐史未敘者，不在焉。

translations.literal: All these were gateways into office; chief recorders of offices already made officials and prefectural and county aides not yet registered were not included.
translations.idiomatic: These were all gateways to office, not counting existing chief recorders or unregistered local aides.

sentences.zh: 至於銓選，其制不一，凡流外，兵部、禮部舉人，郎官得自主之，謂之「小選」。

translations.literal: As for evaluation and selection, its systems were not uniform; for all outside the stream, War and Rites examination graduates, and aide officials could decide independently—called "small selection."
translations.idiomatic: Evaluation systems varied: extra-stream candidates, war and rites graduates, and aides could be appointed independently—the "small selection."

sentences.zh: 太宗時，以歲旱穀貴，東人選者集於洛州，謂之「東選」。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Taizong, because of yearly drought and costly grain, eastern candidates assembled at Luozhou—called "eastern selection."
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong, drought and costly grain led eastern candidates to assemble at Luozhou—the "eastern selection."

sentences.zh: 高宗上元二年，以嶺南五管、黔中都督府得即任土人，而官或非其才，乃遣郎官、御史為選補使，謂之「南選」。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan under Emperor Gaozong, because the five southern circuits and Qianzhong Area Command could immediately employ natives yet offices might not suit their talent, aide officials and censors were sent as selection and supplement commissioners—called "southern selection."
translations.idiomatic: In Gaozong's Shangyuan 2, because the south could appoint locals who were not always capable, aides and censors were sent as selection commissioners—the "southern selection."

sentences.zh: 其後江南、淮南、福建大抵因歲水旱，皆遣選補使即選其人。

translations.literal: Later Jiangnan, Huainan, and Fujian mostly because of yearly flood and drought all sent selection commissioners to choose men on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jiangnan, Huainan, and Fujian likewise sent commissioners to select candidates locally after floods or drought.

sentences.zh: 而廢置不常，選法又不著，故不復詳焉。

translations.literal: Yet abolition and establishment were not constant, and selection law was not written down, so it is not detailed further.
translations.idiomatic: These practices were irregular and undocumented, so they are not described further here.
